key_insight: fTNN is a deterministic tensor neural network framework that combines geometry-aware fractional Laplacian integration with singularity-aware trial functions to solve fractional PDEs accurately on bounded domains.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable alternative to stochastic PINN-style methods for engineering models with nonlocal operators, boundary singularities, and time-dependent fractional dynamics.
method: Split the fractional Laplacian into near-field, interior far-field, and analytical exterior far-field terms using a spatially dependent near-field radius.
Evaluate singular, regular, and angular integrals with Gauss-Jacobi, Gauss, and deterministic angular quadrature, respectively.
Use boundary-singularity-aware trial functions and a spatiotemporally separable network with alternating subspace optimization for time-dependent problems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high accuracy on benchmark fractional Poisson and fractional advection-diffusion problems, with substantial gains over fPINN and Monte Carlo baselines, especially for strong boundary singularities and long-time simulations.
watch_item: Performance depends on correctly estimating the singularity exponent and on the added complexity of deterministic quadrature and alternating optimization in higher dimensions.
paper_title: fTNN: a tensor neural network for fractional PDEs
